correctness.rationale: Exact definitions and quantifiers are fixed. Two independent exhaustive algorithms inspect all n! permutations for 1<=n<=7 and all factor intervals of all intermediate words, build the complete legal swap graph and compute every-pair distances; both report the identical 20-pair exceptional spectrum at n=7 and none earlier. An explicitly verified six-edge path connects the witness; any Kendall-length-four path must first make a single forbidden swap (the resulting word 1000101 violates prefix normality), and parity rules out length five. Prepending new maxima is proved admissibility-preserving, extending the exact four-versus-six distance to every n>=7. Finite enumeration is used only for its stated finite range.

value.rationale: The question is motivated by an explicit literature investigation of legal adjacent swaps between prefix-normal word-chain generators; preserving unrestricted shortest routes is a natural stronger reconfiguration property than mere connectivity. A sharp first failure at length seven, its complete 20-pair joint metric census, and an explicit obstruction persisting at every higher length identify structural boundaries beyond routine relabeling or arbitrary finite slice. The result is not claimed to provide a closed all-length spectrum.
